main_body: Two-storey half-timbered tavern: a large orange tile roof (rows 0-43) over a cream plaster wall with timber frame, shuttered windows, a plank door and a stone base (rows 44-95)
top_band: Orange roof tile slope with a lighter ridge band at rows 0-3, tile courses continuing to the eave at row ~42; the slope is a clearly visible foreshortened top surface about 43 rows tall
evidence: Down the middle column: lit ridge, then roof tile courses with per-tile highlights down to a light eave edge at row ~42, then a darker wall top directly under the overhang. The wall face (rows 44-95) has its own timber, plaster and stone-base shading. The roof reads as a big sloped top surface, as on the reference houses. The door has a dark inner frame on top and left, and the windows have shutters and sills, so the front is set in rather than flat. No receding side faces.

style.evidence: The roof has about 5 tone steps with per-tile highlights and dark gap shadows. The plaster has speckle and stains, the timber is dark brown, the stone base is shaded stone by stone, and the door has plank grain. The outer silhouette outline is very dark, close to near-black, but the interior forms are separated by dark brown timber and value. Per-tile information is comparable to the Beodeul house references, so it would sit acceptably next to them.
